group_assessment.group: Aldaz laboratory, Department of Epigenetics and Molecular Carcinogenesis, MD Anderson Cancer Center, with Noebels (Baylor, video-EEG) and Fonken (UT Austin, behaviour) as method collaborators.
group_assessment.primary_for_the_gene: YES, measured: PubMed 2026-09-13, `Aldaz CM[Author]` returns 138 records and `Aldaz CM[Author] AND WWOX` returns 38, so roughly 28% of the senior author's indexed output is on this gene, and this group reported the WWOX-PPxY binding biology the paper's own premise rests on.
group_assessment.primary_for_the_disease: WEAKER, and the distinction is the point. SCAR12 as a clinical entity was delineated by Gribaa and Mallaret; this group's contribution is the causal molecular mechanism and now the mouse. For the DISEASE the group is a mechanism laboratory, not the clinical describer, so its phenotype OBSERVATIONS carry the weight of an experienced WWOX laboratory while its extrapolation to human SCAR12 severity is an interpretation resting on someone else's clinical series.
group_assessment.observation_vs_interpretation: Observation weighted HIGH: the model, the pull-down, the EEG and the histology are this group's own instruments and the EEG arm is Noebels', an epilepsy electrophysiology laboratory. Interpretation weighted LOWER in two specific places found in this reading - the oligodendrocyte claim its own BRETIGEA panel does not support in hippocampus, and the GABAergic attribution its own hippocampal KEGG panel does not carry.
group_assessment.measured_on: 2026-09-13 via the PubMed MCP connector; counts re-derivable with the two queries quoted above.
group_assessment.weighting: Observation HIGH, interpretation LOWER, and this reading found the seam in two named places. The group has 38 of 138 indexed papers on WWOX and reported the PPxY-binding biology this model's premise rests on, so its instruments - the knock-in, the pull-down, the histology - and Noebels' video-EEG arm are as experienced as this field offers, and the primary observations are weighted accordingly. It is NOT primary for the DISEASE: SCAR12 was clinically delineated by Gribaa 2007 and Mallaret 2014, so every statement of the form 'this phenocopies human SCAR12 severity' is an interpretation resting on another group's clinical series. Two interpretations in this paper are not carried by its own panels - hippocampal oligodendrocyte reduction (Fig. 6c prints p=0.43) and GABAergic suppression attributed to hippocampus (the HPC KEGG panel has no GABAergic row) - which is the predicted shape for a mechanism laboratory reading its own enrichment output generously, and is why the two weights are not one score.

entries.proposition: Wwox^P47T/P47T mice show frequent interictal cortical spike discharges on video-EEG: 0-3098/hour against 0-68/hour in wild type, n=3 per genotype. THE TWO PRINTED RANGES OVERLAP at their lower bound - both start at 0 - so they are not disjoint, and the body text reports neither a mean spike rate nor any statistical test for spike frequency. What the printed numbers support is that no wild-type animal exceeded 68/hour while mutant animals reached 3098/hour; the group means (~30 vs ~2450/hour, n=3, p<0.01) are plotted in Suppl. Fig. S3b and attested at entries[34], not stated in the text; and the categorical separation is seizure occurrence itself (11-22 generalised convulsive seizures in mutants, none in wild type).
entries.snippet: We detected very frequent interictal cortical spike discharges (0–3098/hour)
entries.anchor: Results 2.3, 'WwoxP47T/P47T mice display chronic spontaneous generalized tonic-clonic seizures'

contradicts_locator.what_changed: The clause 'the WT range and the mutant range do not overlap' was FALSE against the paper's own printed ranges: 0-68/hour and 0-3098/hour share their lower bound of 0, so the wild-type range lies wholly inside the mutant range. Replaced with what the printed numbers support. The blind audit then returned OVERSHOOT on the first replacement draft, because it claimed the genotypes are separated by 'the group means' while the BODY TEXT prints no mean spike rate and no statistical test for spike frequency; the means are on Suppl. Fig. S3b, attested by entries[34] of this manifest, not in the text. Final wording names the surface that carries each part.

entries.proposition: ABUNDANCE ARM, and it supports less than it was first read as supporting: the authors state 'similar levels' of Wwox protein in homozygous mutant and wildtype mice, citing the 10% input lane of a pull-down blot at n=2 per genotype (Methods 4.2, whole cerebellar lysates), with NO densitometry anywhere in the paper. What that lane establishes is that Wwox protein is PRESENT in both genotypes; the authors' characterisation of the levels as 'similar' is not independently established by it, and per-lane inspection of the panel shows the two mutant bands somewhat weaker than the two wild-type bands (entries[17]). Protein abundance is therefore NEITHER shown unchanged NOR shown reduced. The transcript arm, which IS quantified, is at entries[35] and entries[54].

entries.proposition: FIG 1a ATTESTS TWO THINGS AT TWO DIFFERENT STRENGTHS. BINDING - near-abolished: Anti-Wwox Dvl2 and Anti-Wwox Wbp1 pulldowns are saturated in both WT/WT lanes and retain only faint residual signal in both P47T/P47T lanes (~3-13% of wild-type integrated density), so the loss of recovery is near-total rather than literally complete. ABUNDANCE - undetermined in direction: the Anti-Wwox 10% input row shows Wwox present in all four lanes with the two P47T/P47T bands thinner and lighter than the two WT/WT bands, against an Anti-Hsp90 loading control that is even to slightly STRONGER in the mutant lanes, so the input deficit is not a loading artefact; at n=2 and with no densitometry in the paper this supports neither comparable abundance nor a quantified reduction.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 1a: four antibody rows over four lanes, two lanes per genotype (WT/WT then P47T/P47T). Anti-Wwox Dvl2 pulldown: bands saturated in both WT lanes, faint residual in both P47T lanes. Anti-Wwox Wbp1 pulldown: same pattern. Anti-Wwox 10% input: bands present in all four lanes, the two P47T/P47T bands visibly thinner and lighter than the two WT/WT bands. Anti-Hsp90: even to slightly stronger in the mutant lanes. Both Anti-Biotin peptide-bead inputs even.
entries.anchor: Figure 1, panel a, native resolution 1801x1412, inspected at native scale and at 3-5x magnification. The abundance evidence is an input lane of a pull-down blot, not a dedicated quantified western; n=2 per genotype is visible as two lanes. CAVEAT ON THE MEASUREMENT: gray value on a JPEG scan of film is not linear in protein, so the per-lane comparisons above are direction and rank order only, never a fold-change.

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Two clauses failed at once. (i) 'Anti-Wwox 10% input shows comparable bands in BOTH genotypes' overstated the panel: the two mutant input bands are thinner and lighter than the two wild-type bands (integrated 1050/1082 vs 1468/1556; half-depth widths 8-9 px vs 10-12 px), while Anti-Hsp90 integrates to 2620/2716 in the mutant lanes against 2447/2510 in wild type, so loading is even to slightly favouring the mutant and the deficit is not a loading artefact. (ii) The replacement draft's 'BINDING: abolished, unambiguous' was itself refused by the blind audit: the mutant pulldown lanes retain FAINT RESIDUAL signal (dipping to gray 149/179 and ~163 against lane backgrounds of ~185-188, roughly 3-13% of wild-type integrated density), so the loss is near-total and not literally complete. The original persisted snippet's 'near-absent' was the accurate word and is restored. The binding half is NOT weakened in substance - only its certainty adverb is corrected.

entries.proposition: THE CITED PANEL DOES NOT SUPPORT THE HIPPOCAMPAL OLIGODENDROCYTE HALF OF THAT SENTENCE AT SIGNIFICANCE: Fig. 6c prints p=0.43 over the HPC OLIGs comparison - the largest p-value in the panel - while HPC OPCs is p=0.02; in PFC the pattern inverts (OLIGs p=0.02, OPCs p=0.27). p=0.43 is non-significance, NOT refutation: the homozygote median is visibly lower and the WT group is dispersed, so the DIRECTION agrees with the text. The text says 'reduced', not 'significantly reduced', and attaches 'significantly' only to astrocytes and microglia.

entries.proposition: THE HIPPOCAMPAL GABAERGIC HALF OF THE SENTENCE IS NOT AMONG THE PATHWAYS ITS CITED PANEL PLOTS: Supplementary Fig. S12 (HPC KEGG; legend mislabelled S11) shows Glutamatergic synapse in the suppressed column and NO GABAergic synapse row among the displayed pathways, while S11 (CTX, page 13) shows both. entries.proposition: THE SUPPLEMENT CITED FOR THE PER-ANIMAL SEIZURE CLAIM SHOWS GROUP MEANS, NOT PER-ANIMAL COUNTS: Supplementary Fig. S3a/b are two-bar graphs of mean seizure number and mean spikes/hour with SEM, n=3 per genotype. They establish the group difference; they do NOT display the individual animals, so 'all three mutants had more than 4 seizures in 24 h' remains attested by the running text alone and cannot be checked against this panel. The running text's per-animal range (11-22 seizures over 43-53 h) is the only individual-level information available, and S3a gives no time window at all, so the panel does not even share the 24 h unit of the claim it is cited for.

entries.proposition: THE CEREBELLAR TRANSCRIPTOME PANEL SHOWS FEWER ANIMALS THAN THE METHODS DECLARE: Fig. 9a and its legend show n=4 WT and n=3 mutant CB samples against the Methods' n=5 per group, the missing leaves being WT M1 and mutant M7 and F9. The text names no excluded samples, though the Methods do state a RIN>8.0 inclusion criterion that could account for them; whether libraries were built and dropped or samples were never sequenced is not stated. The n behind the 1059 cerebellar DEGs is not given, and the clustered set is the likely basis rather than a stated one. Separately, the Methods' sex split of 2 males and 3 females per group contradicts the WT forebrain sample labels in Fig. 6a, which read 3 males and 2 females.

entries.proposition: A COUNTER-DIRECTIONAL TERM INSIDE THE PAPER'S OWN INHIBITION STORY: in Fig. 7a the hippocampal GO term 'inhibitory postsynaptic potential' sits in the ACTIVATED column, black-arrowed, while the KEGG analysis of the same tissue is read by the text as suppression of inhibitory synapses. Two enrichment analyses of one tissue point in opposite directions on inhibition, and the paper reconciles them nowhere. Neither is a measurement of inhibitory transmission.

entries.proposition: THE INFLAMMATORY AXIS IS REGION-WIDE AND CONSISTENT IN SIGN: Fig. 8a places CREB1, TGFB1, TNF, NFkB, IL1A, IL1B, RELA, IL5 and P38 MAPK as activated upstream regulators with positive Z scores in all three forebrain regions, and Fig. 8b shows TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB, IL6_JAK_STAT3_SIGNALING and INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE positively enriched in PFC, CTX and HPC alike. These are transcriptomic inferences about regulators, not measurements of the cytokines themselves.

entries.proposition: A SYSTEMIC NEGATIVE, NOW VERIFIED RATHER THAN CITED: every haematology parameter in Supplementary Table 3 - white cells, neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, basophils, red cells, haemoglobin, haematocrit, indices and platelets - is marked 'ns' across all three genotypes. With Supplementary Table 2's blood chemistry, also uniformly 'ns', the peripheral blood compartment of this model is unremarkable at the ages sampled.

entries.anchor: Supplementary Table 3, p-value column

entries.proposition: THE HETEROZYGOTE IS NOT PHENOTYPE-FREE, AND THE NUMBERS ARE SPECIFIC: Supplementary Table 4 gives the P47T/WT row as 6/19 neoplasia (33%), 4/19 cholestasis (22%), 5/19 focal liver degeneration (28%) and 13/19 nephropathy (72%), against a wild-type row of 2/7 (29%), 0, 0 and 1/7 (14%). Cholestasis and focal liver degeneration are ABSENT in wild type and present in a fifth to a quarter of heterozygotes, and nephropathy is 72% against 14%. No statistical comparison is offered for any of it.
entries.anchor: Supplementary Table 4, heterozygote row

entries.proposition: AND THE HOMOZYGOTE ROW, WHICH IS WHY THE NEOPLASIA NUMBER MUST NOT BE READ AS PROTECTION: Supplementary Table 4 gives P47T/P47T as 1/21 neoplasia (5%), 9/21 cholestasis (43%), 5/21 focal liver degeneration (24%) and 11/21 nephropathy (52%). The low neoplasia figure sits beside a mean survival of 393 days against 542, which is the competing-risk explanation the authors themselves give.
entries.anchor: Supplementary Table 4, homozygote row

entries.proposition: THE STATISTICAL FRAME, AND WHAT IT OMITS: significance is p<0.05 on two-tailed t-tests, Mann-Whitney, or one/two-way ANOVA with Tukey post-hoc. No multiplicity correction across the many endpoints is declared, no power analysis appears anywhere, and no randomisation or blinding is declared for the imaging and quantification work.

entries.proposition: THE GENOTYPE ITSELF IS VERIFIED AT THE SEQUENCE LEVEL: Supplementary Fig. S1c shows Sanger traces for all three genotypes - CCG (Pro) in WT/WT, overlapping C/A and G/C peaks in the heterozygote, ACC (Thr) in the homozygote - and S1b places residue 47 inside the first WW domain of a 405-residue protein whose SDR domain is untouched. The 'partial loss of function' framing is structurally grounded, not asserted.
